title: Heat Pump Rebates in Cambridge 2026: Program Rebates and a 2.5% RetrofitWR Loan
desc: Cambridge heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings, plus a RetrofitWR loan of up to $40,000 at 2.5% for GrandBridge Energy customers.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Cambridge pairs the provincial heat pump rebate with a local loan: GrandBridge Energy customers can borrow up to $40,000 at 2.5% fixed through RetrofitWR for projects that cut energy use by at least 25%.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Cambridge
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

cards.title: RetrofitWR loan
cards.note: Up to $40,000 over 10 or 15 years. For GrandBridge Energy customers in Cambridge and North Dumfries, repaid on the bill, for projects that cut energy use by 25% or more.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: RetrofitWR's loan is repaid on the GrandBridge Energy bill over 10 or 15 years, for customers in Cambridge and North Dumfries. The project must reduce energy use by at least 25%. A heat pump replacing electric baseboards or oil may reach that on its own, while a heat pump added to a gas home may need other measures. Ask the Region what evidence it needs.

The 2021 Census counts 51,270 households in Cambridge. 48% live in homes built before 1981, 57% in detached houses, 77% in an eligible type and 69% own. 12,780 are owner-occupied detached houses of that older era. 5.2% report needing major repairs.

Where a lot has room for a ground loop, ground-source pays $2,000 per ton up to $12,000 for electric, oil, propane and wood homes, or $3,000 flat for gas homes, and the loan can finance the higher upfront cost. Direct-expansion systems are not eligible, and the loop must be sized to the home's load.

The Region's Energy Coach is free for homeowners in Waterloo Region, whether or not they qualify for the loan. Use it to compare quotes, since heat pump sizing and ductwork are the usual sources of disagreement between contractors.

The applicant must own the home and be the person paying for the purchase and installation. A Cambridge owner using the RetrofitWR loan is still the payer, with the loan repaid on the utility bill. Where an owner has tenants, the owner applies, and a tenant cannot apply for the owner.
claim_steps: Ask GrandBridge Energy and the Region about RetrofitWR before you sign a contract.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
